correctness.rationale: Exact order mod odd prime powers is t_p p^max(0,a_p-s_p), so the global p-adic valuation is max(a_p,s_p+h_p), implying sharp odd thresholds. For the binary prime, standard v2(b^(2^k)-1) and the order mod 2^a give the a2=1 exception precisely when b≡3 mod4 and all other local orders are odd. Counting fixed-support exponent vectors reduces to weighted simplex lattice points plus at most one lower-dimensional layer. A separate modular-order verifier passed 3327 cases across bases 2,3,5,7,9,11,13,17; those finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared theorem-level implications, not matching terms. Falk–Harrington–Jones (arXiv:2607.29329v1) establish generalized prime-level Wieferich congruences in a monogenic-trinomial classification, not the condition on all prime powers of composite n. Franco–Pomerance (1995, pp.1333–1336) establish density-one and a local obstruction for odd base-two integers, not a necessary/sufficient fixed-radical exponent region. Siegel (arXiv:2610.28685v1, 19 October 2026, later than the motivating July paper) proves sufficient squarefree conditions and a conditional global asymptotic, which neither supplies full prime-power coverage nor the even-integer exception. A complete general fixed-support theorem was not located in indexed records or the inspected full texts; generic LTE may yield equivalent deductions, so bibliographic risk persists.
residual_risks: An unindexed published treatment of Wieferich integers may derive these thresholds from standard LTE; no exhaustive bibliographic uniqueness proof is claimed.
The classical LTE and modular-order lemmas are major prerequisites; their individual statements are not original.
Siegel appeared on October 19, 2026, after the July 2026 motivating paper. It was checked only for possible mathematical overlap.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural fixed-radical classification for every coprime base, not arbitrary prime slices or isolated numbers. It shows each fixed support has infinitely many non-Wieferich integers even when it contains Wieferich prime factors, and identifies a mathematically sharp dyadic failure of exponent upward closure. The universal logarithmic leading constant quantifies every fixed-radical family; none of this follows from global density alone. Its proof is elementary, which limits claims of depth but does not erase the natural complete classification.
